intro: People love to belong. Kids make clubs in blanket forts. Grown-ups sing in choirs and play on teams. Some meet in lodges. A club is a group that shares something they like or do.

Clubs often have secrets. A password is a secret. A birthday gift is a secret too. Most secrets are safe and happy. But some secrets make you feel worried or scared. Those secrets need a trusted grown-up.
In this unit you will learn what makes a club kind and fair. You will learn to tell a safe secret from an unsafe one. You will name the grown-ups who can help you.
bigQuestion: How can clubs and secrets be kind, fair and safe?

timeline.t: Friends find something they all like to do.
They pick a place to meet, like a blanket fort.
They choose a club name and a symbol.
A new friend asks to join, and the club says welcome.
The club keeps a safe secret, like a password.
Someone has a secret that feels scary or wrong.
They tell a trusted grown-up and get help.

words.d: a group of people who share something they like or do
a person who belongs to a club or group
a picture or sign that stands for something
words that tell people what to do so things are safe and fair
a happy secret that is shared soon and makes someone glad
a secret word you say to show you belong
could hurt someone or make someone scared
someone you can count on to listen and help

choices: A group of people who share something
test.why: A club is a group of people who share something they like or do.

test.q: Where did the Bug Club meet?
test.why: Maya, Omar and Lily made a clubhouse out of a blanket fort.

test.q: What is a good club rule?
test.why: The Bug Club's first rule was that kind people are always welcome. It is fair and kind.
A choir is a group of grown-ups or kids who sing together. Grown-ups have clubs too.

test.q: What did the Moose club open in Illinois in 1913?
choices: A home for children called Mooseheart
test.why: Mooseheart was a home and school for children of Moose members who had died.
A club password hurts no one. It is a safe secret.

test.q: Eli hid a card for Grandma. What kind of secret was it?
test.why: It was a happy secret that ended on her birthday. That is a surprise.

test.q: Your tummy feels tight because of a secret. What can that mean?
test.why: Worried feelings in your body can mean a secret is unsafe. Tell a trusted grown-up.

test.q: Who should you tell about an unsafe secret?
test.why: Any secret about touching, hurting or danger is told to a trusted grown-up.

test.q: A friend is hurt at recess. Is telling a grown-up tattling?
choices: No, it is telling to keep someone safe
test.why: Someone could get hurt. Telling to keep someone safe is not tattling.

write.prompt: Draw or write about a club you would make. What is its name and symbol? Write one fair rule. Then tell one secret your club could keep, and say why it is a safe secret.
tips: Give your club a name and draw its symbol.
Write a rule that is fair to everyone.
Tell how your club will welcome a new member.
Use the words safe secret or surprise.
